The Nigeria Police Force has assured members of the National Youth Service Corps and other ad hoc personnel engaged by the Independent National Electoral Commission of adequate security during the 2027 general elections. This assurance follows two recent incidents: the November 2026 abduction of nine corps members and a commercial driver on the Ijebu-Ode–Ibadan road in Ogun State, and the October 1, 2026 kidnapping of 20 prospective corps members on the Owerri-Onitsha road in Imo State, which has since gone to court. The incidents have renewed concerns over the safety of young Nigerians deployed for national assignments, including election duties, particularly as corps members constitute a significant part of INEC’s ad hoc workforce. Speaking on preparations for the forthcoming general elections at the joint security agencies briefing on Thursday in Abuja, the police spokesman, Ani Iniedu, said the Force had conducted an extensive threat assessment and was strengthening security arrangements to protect electoral personnel. He said the police were working with INEC and other security agencies to ensure that corps members and other temporary electoral workers were adequately protected before, during and after the elections. “In every election cycle, there are potential threats to soft targets. However, as other targets become increasingly fortified, criminals may attempt to exploit perceived vulnerabilities elsewhere. Make PUNCH part of your everyday experience. The forthcoming general election will not be an exception. “We are working closely with sister security agencies through the established inter-agency security arrangements. We are also engaging the Independent National Electoral Commission to ensure adequate protection for corps members and other ad hoc personnel involved in the electoral process,”he said. Iniedu disclosed that they were increasing security deployments ahead of the elections, while the Inspector-General of Police had directed the immediate distribution of operational equipment and logistics. Reassuring corps members and other young Nigerians participating in the electoral process, the police said their safety remained a priority. “I want to assure members of the public, particularly corps members and young Nigerians participating in the electoral process, that their safety remains a priority for the Nigeria Police Force. “We will do everything within our capacity to ensure that those assisting in the democratic process are adequately protected,” he added. Meanwhile, the force spokesmanwarned political actors against hate speech, incitement and other forms of political violence capable of undermining the electoral process. He disclosed that the police had documented about 11 reported cases of hate speech and the actions taken on them. Iniedu said the Inspector-General had directed all Commissioners of Police to ensure the immediate arrest and prosecution of individuals involved in such offences. “Hate speech and incitement are criminal offences. The Inspector-General of Police has directed all Commissioners of Police to ensure the immediate arrest and prosecution of individuals involved in such acts,” he said. He added that the police had established complaint channels through which members of the public could report Commissioners of Police who failed to take appropriate action against offenders. “We will be taking decisive action against offenders.We have also established complaint channels to ensure that where a Commissioner of Police fails to take appropriate action, such failures can be reported and addressed, ” he said.
